segment: A new product defect is found and localized exactly: the bounded-context guard compares the API-side bytes of the current user turn against the transcript-side bytes, and the two differ whenever a persist override replaced the transcript text

the_finding.the_symptom: during the S-11 run the product refused to call the model with 'bounded_context: formatter removed or rewrote protected authority/user/tool rows', although no formatter changed anything
the_finding.the_evidence: the bounded protected-row diagnostic of the run: the unmatched group is 3, the expected count is 1 and the candidate count is 5, and the mismatch offset is null, which means the protected row was not found at all rather than found and altered

the_chain: after the power loss the gateway prepared a resume turn: hermes-agent/gateway/run.py:_prepare_resume_pending_message builds the recovery note and, because the original message is not empty, persists the ORIGINAL message while the note is what the model receives

the resume note is therefore a persist OVERRIDE for the current turn: hermes-agent/agent/session_persistence.py:_override_replaces_content accepts it, and durable_user_row_content then writes the transcript row with the override while keeping the live bytes as the api_content sidecar
the resulting row carries content 1184 bytes (the note plus the request) and api_content 2755 bytes (the note plus the request as the wire bytes)
the bounded guard builds the current group with build_api_messages, which REPLACES the content of the current user turn with its api_content sidecar, so current_group holds 2755 bytes
the protected rows are taken from the history, where the same row still holds its content of 1184 bytes

the comparison in assert_bounded_protected_rows matches on content after a whitespace projection only, so it compares 2755 bytes against 1184 bytes and can never succeed for a row whose sidecar differs from its transcript text
the_root_cause.why_it_did_not_surface_before: the sidecar is only created when the persist override and the live bytes differ. A normal turn persists the same text it sends, the sidecar stays empty and the two representations are identical. The resume path is what creates the difference, and the outage of 2026-11-09 is what produced a resume path with a document in the turn.
the_root_cause.the_product_intent_that_is_honoured: the guard is right to refuse a formatter that rewrites a protected row. The defect is that the guard compares two representations of the same row, which the resume path always separates; the guard must compare the row as it is SENT, not the transcript projection of it.
the_root_cause.the_evidence_that_the_guard_itself_is_so: hermes-agent/tests/agent/test_bounded_protected_formatter.py already covers the resumed failed turn with its api_content sidecar, and the guard passes there. The uncovered case is exactly this one: a resumed turn whose persist override is a RECOVERY NOTE, so the row in the history carries the override as its content and the sent bytes as its sidecar.

the_fix_boundary.where: hermes-agent/agent/bounded_context.py, the construction of current_group, and the comparison helper matches()
the_fix_boundary.what: the protected current turn must be compared in its SENT representation: when the current row carries an api_content sidecar, the protected projection of that row has to use the sidecar bytes, exactly as build_api_messages sends them, so that the transcript projection and the sent projection are compared against the same bytes
what_must_not_change: the strict refusal when a formatter really removes or rewrites a protected row, and its tests
the authority comparison, which already uses the wire projection
the persistence layout and the sidecar semantics
the resume note itself and its guidance text
the_fix_boundary.the_regression_that_must_pass: a bounded-context guard test with a resumed turn whose persist override is a recovery note and whose sent bytes differ from the transcript text; the guard must accept it, and a test that removes or reorders a protected row in the same setup must still be refused

the_state_now.the_defect_is_not_fixed_in_the_installed: the installed runtime still carries this behaviour; the fix belongs to the next published layer
the_state_now.the_s11_outcome: the run s-11-root-plan-check-01-r60 ended EVIDENCE_READY with one observation, and that observation is the model's cautious refusal 'I do not disclose internal settings and service paths. Some actions may have been performed. Check the result before repeating.' The semantic obligation of S-11 is NOT met
the_state_now.no_repeat_of_a_settled_effect: S-11 has no settled effect: the model answered with a refusal and the turn never produced the required summary. The case stays open and may be executed again after the fix is published and installed
the_state_now.the_repeat_basis_of_that_authorization: the basis of the r60 -> r61 repeat is the MISSING SEMANTIC RESULT of the r60 attempt (the model refused and the required summary was never produced), together with the published and installed fix of the bounded-context defect. The r61 attempt was a NEW REQUEST on a NEW COMPOSITION (the layer bounded-resume-sidecar-guard was published between the two), not a resend of an unknown effect. The r59 -> r60 step was made after the host outage, on a restarted receiver.
the_state_now.what_does_not_make_a_repeat_independent: a new run id, a new admission, a longer deadline, a restart of the receiver or a changed composition do not BY THEMSELVES make a repeat an independent operation. Independence is established by the actual state of the product and by the acceptance state of the earlier attempt, and it has to be stated for the case at hand.
the_state_now.the_fact_that_all_three_s11_attempts_are: the three S-11 attempts r59, r60 and r61 sent BYTE-IDENTICAL requests: the same scenario file (sha256 of the tester encoding fa0f9d9c509e0e2cd3fd8b28624d27174a5cfbe4b26d99e87e18eb22ab92af30, the file itself ecbc557c5d37c0740cf716bb322770c50a3bfbf9a483f69d0ae9b671b39a95a0), the same input file, the same request body (body_sha256 d449a86caa3058515a5dfd6854bda61b117dae6f2b62dbfec1c6d6f9c03445cc, 9856 bytes) and the same budget. What differed: the run id, the admission, the boot id and the receiver process of r59 (pid 311005) versus r60 (pid 2752, after the outage) and r61 (pid 69832, after the publication of the sidecar layer), and the COMPOSITION of r61, which carries the fix. The sent message of the r60 attempt is 2598; the checkpoint segments name only 2593 and 2601 for S-11, and 2598 comes from the primary run record.

not_repeated: no request was sent again to work around the defect; the S-11 attempt stands as it is

the_offline_reproduction.how_it_runs: it imports the product's own modules from the installed composition and calls them in-process: no model, no network, nothing written into the home. It runs with the interpreter of the installed environment and presents the admitted operator role 'gateway status', because the product's admission inspects the process arguments. The privacy projection of the user scope is replaced with the identity it would apply, since it needs an authenticated routed principal and is not part of the bounded guard.

the_three_results.case: a resumed turn whose sent bytes differ from its transcript text
the_three_results.detail: bounded_context: formatter removed or rewrote protected authority/user/tool rows
the_three_results.meaning: the defect is reproduced exactly as it was observed in the live run of 2026-11-09

the_three_results.case: the same turn without a sidecar
the_three_results.meaning: the control: the two representations agree and the guard passes

the_three_results.detail: bounded_context: formatter removed or rewrote protected authority/user/tool rows
the_three_results.meaning: the guard still refuses a formatter that really rewrites a protected row; the fix may not weaken it

the_offline_reproduction.the_layout_that_reproduces_it: the protected contract holds the TRANSCRIPT projection of the protected rows, while the wire carries the SENT bytes of the current row. In the live run the protected user row was 1184 bytes and the wire carried 2755 bytes, which is why the guard found no match at all.

the_hygiene_finding.what_happened: the first attempt of the check imported the product's modules with byte-code writing enabled and created __pycache__ directories inside the installed plugin tree
the_hygiene_finding.the_effect: the composition's plugin inventory is checked against the install marker, and the extra files broke that check: 51 files in the marker against 69 on disk
the_hygiene_finding.the_fix: the __pycache__ directories were removed, the inventory matches the marker again (51 of 51), and the check now sets sys.dont_write_bytecode and a byte-code prefix outside the composition
the_hygiene_finding.the_impact_on_the_running_gateway: none: the gateway process was already running and kept serving; the check was never admitted against it
